Purification by holy words.

The priest's exorcism scatters Zouken Matou's spirit into mist.

Only two figures remain in the square:

Kirei Kotomine, his black vestments dyed scarlet, leaning battered against the wall—

and the skeletal Assassin, pinned to a great tree by Black Keys.

“Why Zabaniya failed.

“That arm appears to be a gift from the Devil. But so long as Zabaniya bears the name of an angel of Hell, it can have no effect upon me.

That arm punishes humans, so it cannot curse one of its own kind. As my heart is not human, it is strong against such a curse.”

Zouken's wish was eternal youth and immortality.

For that, the body of Sakura Matou, transformed into the Holy Grail, would have been enough.

While that old man lived, the “curse” conceived within the Grail could never hatch.

There would be no point in letting Sakura Matou mature this far only to become a vessel for Zouken.

Sakura Matou must remain as she is: its host, its “Master.”

Because that—

“Born lacking it——”

After accepting that truth, the man made every conceivable effort.

Though incapable of comprehending morality, he possessed common sense. His entire youth was devoted to overcoming that defect.

But he never succeeded.

His ordeals and anguish brought him no relief. Every effort ended in vain.

His final attempt was a single woman.

pages.en:
It was a simple matter.

Whatever kind of person one may be, no one entirely fails to imagine loving another, building a family, and quietly breathing their last.

Even those who despise such peace cannot help but dream of it.

The man was no exception.

Though he found not the slightest appeal in it, he wished that he might be capable of such a life.

And so, in pursuit of an ordinary happiness, he loved a woman.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s a simple story.
Every human wishes to love one of the opposite sex, have a family, and die peacefully.
Even if one may detest the peace, one can only dream about it.
This man is no exception.
He wished for such a thing, even though he felt no fascination in it.
He loved a woman, trying to earn ordinary happiness.

The woman he chose had no future.

Disease had consumed her. She could have had only a few years left to live.

Did he choose her because she was such a woman, or was she the only kind of woman he could choose?

Even now, looking back, he cannot say.

pages.en:
Their life together lasted roughly two years.

The man tried to love the woman.

She, too, strove to love him. She did love him, and bore him a child.

But the outcome did not change.

For what brought happiness to the man was the woman's suffering—and his own child's despair.

The harder he tried to love them, the more the suffering of those he loved became his only salvation.
